title: The Night-Adventure of Sultan Mohammed of Cairo
summary: One moonless night, Sultan Mohammed of Cairo slipped out of the Citadel disguised as an ordinary municipal guard, carrying a sturdy oak cudgel and a hooded lantern.
keywords: the night-adventure of sultan mohammed of cairo
full_text:
One moonless night, Sultan Mohammed of Cairo slipped out of the Citadel disguised as an ordinary municipal guard, carrying a sturdy oak cudgel and a hooded lantern.

As he traversed the quiet alleys near the Bab Zuweila gate, he heard muffled cries of distress coming from a deserted courtyard. Peering through a broken wooden lattice, he saw four armed ruffians surrounding a lone traveling merchant and his young daughter, demanding their baggage of silks.

Without hesitating, the Sultan kicked open the decayed gate, raised his lantern high, and shouted with thunderous authority:
'Stand fast in the name of Justice!'

The bandits, seeing only a single guard, mocked him and drew their scimitars. But Sultan Mohammed was a master swordsman. With swift, powerful strokes of his cudgel, he disarmed the first two, tripped the third, and pinned the fourth against the stone wall.

The city patrol, alerted by the clamor, rushed into the courtyard and bound the brigands. The captain of the patrol, not recognizing the disguised Sultan in the shadows, praised him:
'Well fought, comrade! Who art thou that handlest a cudgel like an imperial general?'

The Sultan smiled: 'I am a humble servant of Cairo who believes that the night belongs to peaceful citizens, not to jackals.'

The grateful merchant fell to his knees, offering a purse of gold coins: 'Noble guardian, take this reward, for thou hast saved my life and my daughter's honor!'

The Sultan gently raised the old man:
'Keep thy gold, merchant, to trade fairly in our markets. The protection of honest travelers is not bought with coins; it is the sacred debt every strong arm owes to the defenseless.'

The next morning, the Sultan summoned the merchant and his daughter to the palace. When the merchant saw the Sultan seated on the throne, he gasped, recognizing the heroic guardian of the night!
The Sultan restored all their goods, punished the bandits with labor on the city ramparts, and established night lanterns along every alley in Cairo, demonstrating that true kings watch while their people sleep in peace.
moral: Courage in the dark and vigilance in defense of the innocent are the sacred duties of righteous leadership.
